scale.1: Strong concern: significant gaps; would not pass this dimension at the target level.
scale.2: Below bar: partially demonstrated, shallow, or needed heavy steering.
scale.3: At bar: solid and well reasoned with minor gaps; meets senior expectations.
scale.4: Above bar: drove the discussion, went deep, and showed staff-level judgment.

dimensions.name: Requirements & scoping
dimensions.signals: Clarified functional and non-functional requirements; asked for scale; did back-of-the-envelope estimates (QPS, storage, bandwidth); scoped the problem to what matters.

levels.1: No clarification; designed for an unstated problem.
levels.2: Some requirements gathered but missed key non-functional needs or never estimated.
levels.3: Clear functional and non-functional requirements with reasonable estimates that informed the design.
levels.4: Crisp scoping, prioritized requirements, and estimates that directly drove decisions.

dimensions.name: High-level design
dimensions.signals: Coherent architecture with clear components and data flow; APIs defined; data model defined; diagram communicates the design.

levels.2: Plausible components but unclear data flow, APIs, or data model.
levels.3: Complete and coherent design with APIs, data model, and a clear diagram.
levels.4: Elegant, well-justified design; every component has a clear reason to exist.

dimensions.name: Deep dive & technical depth
dimensions.signals: Went deep on the hardest components (e.g. ID generation, consistency, caching, partitioning); showed real knowledge of the technologies chosen; handled the follow-up probes.

levels.2: Some depth, but with technical errors or gaps when probed.
levels.3: Solid depth on key components with correct technical reasoning.
levels.4: Expert depth; anticipated subtle issues and proposed robust solutions.

dimensions.name: Scalability, reliability & tradeoffs
dimensions.signals: Identified bottlenecks and single points of failure; discussed scaling (sharding, replication, caching, queues); explicit tradeoffs (consistency vs availability, latency vs accuracy, cost); failure modes and monitoring.

levels.1: No discussion of scale or failure.
levels.2: Generic scaling remarks not tied to this system's bottlenecks.
levels.3: Found the real bottlenecks and made reasoned tradeoffs.
levels.4: Thorough treatment of failure modes, tradeoffs, and operational concerns, with sound judgment.

dimensions.name: Communication & leadership
dimensions.signals: Drove the conversation with structure; checked in with the interviewer; responded to pushback; follow-up answers were clear.

levels.1: Disorganized; the interviewer had to drive.
levels.4: Led confidently with excellent structure and time management.
